# Backspace Fork 1.15.1

This release adds an opt-in Windows HDR-to-SDR screen-sharing pipeline, plus an optional instance-owned minimum desktop version with a mandatory update/recovery screen. Browser access remains available and account credentials, drafts and resumable transfers are preserved.

## What's new

- **Force SDR:** saved per device and off by default. Windows capture uses high-precision Windows Graphics Capture, GPU peak measurement, tone mapping and color management to produce the SDR video track without switching off the monitor's HDR. Preview and publication use the same corrected track. Changing the choice recreates a staged preview; an active share must be stopped and restarted.
- **Desktop compatibility:** operators can configure `BACKSPACE_MIN_DESKTOP_VERSION`. The entire updated application waits for compatibility before starting ordinary session effects. An outdated desktop gets update progress, ready-only compatible installation, manual/package-manager guidance, trusted installer downloads and a browser recovery path. API/raw uploads/WebSockets consistently refuse identifiable incompatible human desktops; verified bots and ordinary browsers remain available.
- **Release integrity:** one publisher assembles all platform artifacts, checks complete updater references and hashes, and publishes a single exact release id. Conflicting existing assets/notes fail instead of being overwritten. Windows packages require the native addon matching their architecture and retain the existing Electron security fuses.

## Acceptance limitations

The operator requested publication and deployment for real-world testing before hardware and historical-host acceptance could be completed. These are **not claimed as passing**: real HDR-monitor-to-SDR-receiver comparison, sustained capture resource measurements, ARM64 GPU capture, installed-package acceptance, and original 1.14.2/1.15.0 updater/service-worker/active-call transitions. Matching-host native build/module-load/unpacked-package tests are distinct from those hardware checks.

The desktop minimum is **disabled by default**. REST/WS refusal and updated-renderer teardown do not prove termination of an independently valid LiveKit media grant held by an old cached bundle across a server restart. Operators should validate recovery and active-call behavior before enabling enforcement. macOS ad-hoc signed builds still require manual updates; package-manager builds remain externally managed. This policy is not device attestation or an authorization boundary.
